elements.texte:
[cheerful] New lesson: comparing against a whole list.

Compare a value to all of a subquery’s values, or to at least one.
elements.apres: The NutriBoost shop is launching a premium range.
phrases: New lesson: comparing against a whole list.
Compare a value to all of a subquery’s values, or to at least one.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] The NutriBoost shop is launching a premium range.

The team wants to put in it the products more expensive than all the products in the Wellness category.

To show them, we get the products’ name and price from the products table.

The prices of the Wellness category are in the same table.
elements.avant: Compare a value to all of a subquery’s values, or to at least one.
elements.apres: A subquery reads the price of the products in the Wellness category: it returns three values.
phrases: The NutriBoost shop is launching a premium range.
The team wants to put in it the products more expensive than all the products in the Wellness category.
To show them, we get the products’ name and price from the products table.
The prices of the Wellness category are in the same table.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] A subquery reads the price of the products in the Wellness category: it returns three values.

€29.90 for Prebiotic Fiber, €19.90 for Magnesium and €24.90 for Omega 3.

But greater than compares a price to a single value.

With three values, you need to say how to compare.

More expensive than all the values, or more expensive than at least one?

That’s what ALL and ANY are for.
elements.avant: The prices of the Wellness category are in the same table.
elements.apres: Greater than ALL is true if the price is greater than each of the values of the subquery.
phrases: A subquery reads the price of the products in the Wellness category: it returns three values.
€29.90 for Prebiotic Fiber, €19.90 for Magnesium and €24.90 for Omega 3.
But greater than compares a price to a single value.
With three values, you need to say how to compare.
More expensive than all the values, or more expensive than at least one?
That’s what ALL and ANY are for.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Greater than ALL is true if the price is greater than each of the values of the subquery.

So the price must be above €29.90, €19.90 and €24.90.

Let’s take Plant Protein, at €34.90.

All three comparisons are true: ALL is true.

Now let’s take Omega 3, at €24.90.

Its price isn’t above €29.90: one false comparison is enough, ALL is false.

With greater than ALL, only two products remain: the most expensive ones.
elements.avant: That’s what ALL and ANY are for.
elements.apres: Greater than ANY is true if the price is above at least one value of the subquery.
phrases: Greater than ALL is true if the price is greater than each of the values of the subquery.
So the price must be above €29.90, €19.90 and €24.90.
Let’s take Plant Protein, at €34.90.
All three comparisons are true: ALL is true.
Now let’s take Omega 3, at €24.90.
Its price isn’t above €29.90: one false comparison is enough, ALL is false.
With greater than ALL, only two products remain: the most expensive ones.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Greater than ANY is true if the price is above at least one value of the subquery.

This time, Omega 3, at €24.90, is above €19.90: ANY is true.

Magnesium, at €19.90, isn’t above any of the three values: ANY is false.

Product by product, ALL keeps 2 products, and ANY keeps 4.

With greater than ANY, it’s enough to be above the cheapest one in the Wellness category.

And equals ANY amounts to in: equal to at least one value in the list.
elements.avant: With greater than ALL, only two products remain: the most expensive ones.
elements.apres: The same query can also be written without ANY or ALL.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] The same query can also be written without ANY or ALL.

We get the same result by comparing to a single value.

Greater than all the values means greater than the largest one: max of price.

Greater than at least one value means greater than the smallest one: min of price.

And instead of equals ANY, we write in.
elements.avant: And equals ANY amounts to in: equal to at least one value in the list.
elements.apres: The complete query is written with greater than ALL.

[cheerful] The complete query is written with greater than ALL.

Or with max of price, which returns €29.90, the largest value.

Both give 2 rows: Marine Collagen and Plant Protein.

The two selected products join the premium range.
